documents.title: Getting started
documents.description: This guide takes you from a clean checkout to a running service with an owner key and a narrow RazorBills integration key.

documents.title: Configuration
documents.description: All configuration is environment-driven and validated at startup by src/config/env.js. The canonical template is ../.env.example.

documents.title: Architecture
documents.description: One stateful dependency: the filesystem. No database, no Redis, no ORM, no migrations. Everything is a JSON/JSONL file or an encrypted blob under DATA_DIR.

documents.title: Owner dashboard (ww2web)

documents.title: Authentication
documents.description: Every /api/v1 route except the Meta webhook receiver requires an API key in the X-API-Key header. A key is never accepted in a query string or path, so it cannot end up in access logs, proxies, referrers or browser hi…

documents.title: API reference
documents.description: Base path: /api/v1. Unless stated otherwise every route requires an X-API-Key header carrying a key with the listed scope.

documents.title: Connectors
documents.description: A connector is the adapter between the gateway's stable API and a specific WhatsApp transport. Business logic never imports a WhatsApp library directly: it talks to the interface in src/connectors/connector.interface.js.

documents.title: Connection lifecycle
documents.description: Each instance owns one connector session. The connection state is explicit, persisted, and recoverable across restarts.

documents.title: Outbound messaging
documents.description: The RazorBills backend sends messages through a single endpoint with the narrow messages:send scope.

documents.title: Real-time events (SSE)
documents.description: Live connection status and authentication challenges are delivered over Server-Sent Events (SSE).

documents.title: Storage
documents.description: There is no database and no Redis. Everything the service persists lives under DATA_DIR (default ./data).

documents.title: Data retention and privacy
documents.description: The gateway collects only what it needs and keeps message content off disk unless the operator explicitly opts in.

documents.title: Security
documents.description: This service is private and single-owner. The security properties below are enforced in code and covered by tests under tests/security/ and tests/integration/.

documents.title: Operations
documents.description: A runbook for running, maintaining and troubleshooting the service.

documents.title: Deployment
documents.description: The default image is lean: only the official Cloud API connector ships.
